# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm generate` from the td2d command definitions. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command accepts the global options below. With `--json`, stdout carries exactly one JSON envelope
(`{ ok, command, version, durationMs, data, warnings, error? }`) and stderr carries NDJSON logs and progress.
Exit codes and every error code are in the [error reference](errors.md); `td2d explain <code>` prints one entry.

## Global options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-V, --version` | Print the td2d version |
| `--project <dir>` | Project root (default: nearest directory with td2d.project.json) |
| `--json` | Print one JSON envelope on stdout; NDJSON logs and progress on stderr |
| `--log-level <level>` | Log verbosity. One of `silent`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`. Default `"info"`. |
| `--no-color` | Disable colour (also honours NO_COLOR) |

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`td2d init`](#td2d-init) | Create a td2d project from a template. |
| [`td2d doctor`](#td2d-doctor) | Check that this machine can run td2d: Node.js, native modules, the headless browser and the project. |
| [`td2d schema`](#td2d-schema) | Print the JSON Schema for a document type, list document types, or write every schema to a directory. |
| [`td2d describe`](#td2d-describe) | Describe everything this version of td2d supports: commands, documents, part types, presets, palettes, templates and error codes. |
| [`td2d validate`](#td2d-validate) | Validate asset definitions (config), or also build and check their geometry (model), without rendering. |
| [`td2d asset list`](#td2d-asset-list) | List every asset in the project with its schema status. |
| [`td2d asset show`](#td2d-asset-show) | Show an asset after defaults and presets are applied. |
| [`td2d asset emit`](#td2d-asset-emit) | Run a TypeScript asset script and write the definition it returns to assets/<id>/asset.json. |
| [`td2d asset create`](#td2d-asset-create) | Scaffold assets/<id>/asset.json from a template. |
| [`td2d generate`](#td2d-generate) | Run the full pipeline: build the model, render every direction and frame, make sprites and a sheet, validate, and export. |
| [`td2d batch`](#td2d-batch) | Generate many assets with a concurrency limit and one shared browser, writing build/batch-report.json. |
| [`td2d model build`](#td2d-model-build) | Build the model GLB for an asset, with its rig and baked clips (the resolve, model and rig stages). |
| [`td2d model inspect`](#td2d-model-inspect) | Report bounds, triangle counts, materials, parts, bones, clips and glTF validation for an asset model, building it if needed. |
| [`td2d rig list`](#td2d-rig-list) | List rig presets: built in and from presets/rig/. |
| [`td2d rig show`](#td2d-rig-show) | Show the bones of an asset rig with their rest positions, and the parts attached to each. |
| [`td2d process`](#td2d-process) | Rerun pixel processing and every later stage from the cached renders. |
| [`td2d sheet`](#td2d-sheet) | Lay out the sheets again from the cached sprites, then validate and export. |
| [`td2d export`](#td2d-export) | Write export formats from the cached sheets. |
| [`td2d render`](#td2d-render) | Render an asset (pipeline stages up to render) or a GLB file to transparent PNG frames, one per direction and sample time. |
| [`td2d inspect`](#td2d-inspect) | Summarise the last generation of an asset: sheet, cells, pivot, validation and stages. |
| [`td2d preview`](#td2d-preview) | Write an enlarged PNG of the sheet on a visible background with cell borders, for viewing with an image reader. |
| [`td2d history list`](#td2d-history-list) | List recorded generations of an asset, newest first. |
| [`td2d history show`](#td2d-history-show) | Show one recorded generation: its sheets, cells, clips, failing checks, timing and size on disk. |
| [`td2d history prune`](#td2d-history-prune) | Remove old history entries: beyond the newest --keep of each asset, older than --older-than, or both. |
| [`td2d cache stats`](#td2d-cache-stats) | Size of the cache by stage and item kind, with the oldest and newest use. |
| [`td2d cache clean`](#td2d-cache-clean) | Remove cache entries by age or size, least recently used first. |
| [`td2d compare`](#td2d-compare) | Compare the current build of an asset with an earlier generation, cell by cell: changed pixels per cell, added and removed cells, and an optional diff image. |
| [`td2d viewer`](#td2d-viewer) | Serve the read-only web viewer for this project's build directory until interrupted. |
| [`td2d index`](#td2d-index) | Write the viewer as a static site into build/ (index.html, index.json and _td2d/) so any static file server can show the build without td2d. |
| [`td2d explain`](#td2d-explain) | Explain an error or warning code: what it means, when it happens, how to fix it and where to read more. |
| [`td2d completion`](#td2d-completion) | Print a shell completion script for bash, zsh or fish: commands, options, option values and asset ids. |

<a id="td2d-init"></a>

### td2d init

Create a td2d project from a template. Never overwrites existing files.

```sh
td2d init [options] [dir]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[dir]` | Directory to create the project in. Default `"."`. |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--template <name>` | Project template (starter). Default `"starter"`. |
| `--name <name>` | Project name written to td2d.project.json (default: directory name) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d init my-sprites
td2d init . --name "Forest tiles" --json
```

<a id="td2d-doctor"></a>

### td2d doctor

Check that this machine can run td2d: Node.js, native modules, the headless browser and the project.

```sh
td2d doctor [options]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--fix` | Install the headless browser if it is missing |

Examples:

```sh
td2d doctor
td2d doctor --fix --json
```

Exit code 7 means a check failed; each failed check has a code and a hint.

<a id="td2d-schema"></a>

### td2d schema

Print the JSON Schema for a document type, list document types, or write every schema to a directory.

```sh
td2d schema [options] [name]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[name]` | Document type, such as asset or project |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--list` | List document types |
| `--write <dir>` | Write every schema to <dir> as <name>.schema.json |

Examples:

```sh
td2d schema --list
td2d schema asset > asset.schema.json
td2d schema --write .td2d/schemas
```

Without --json the schema itself is printed, so the output is a valid JSON Schema document.

<a id="td2d-describe"></a>

### td2d describe

Describe everything this version of td2d supports: commands, documents, part types, presets, palettes, templates and error codes.

```sh
td2d describe [options] [section]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[section]` | Only this part of the description, such as partTypes, presets, pixelPasses or errors |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--schemas` | Include the JSON Schema of every entry |

Examples:

```sh
td2d describe --json
td2d describe partTypes --json
td2d describe presets --json --schemas
```

Sections: version, documents, partTypes, directions, presets, palettes, templates, backends, rigs, generators, easings, easingDocs, pixelPasses, exporters, stages, exitCodes, errors, warnings, cli.

<a id="td2d-validate"></a>

### td2d validate

Validate asset definitions (config), or also build and check their geometry (model), without rendering.

```sh
td2d validate [options] [ids...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[ids...]` | Asset ids to validate (default: every asset) |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--stage <stage>` | config: definitions, presets and palettes. model: also build geometry and check it against the frame. One of `config`, `model`. Default `"config"`. |

Examples:

```sh
td2d validate
td2d validate props/crate --json
td2d validate --stage model --json
```

Exit code 3 means at least one definition or model is invalid. Every issue has a file and a path.

<a id="td2d-asset-list"></a>

### td2d asset list

List every asset in the project with its schema status.

```sh
td2d asset list [options]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ids` | Print only the asset ids, one per line, without reading the definitions (used by shell completion) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d asset list --json
td2d asset list --ids
```

<a id="td2d-asset-show"></a>

### td2d asset show

Show an asset after defaults and presets are applied.

```sh
td2d asset show [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id, such as props/crate |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--raw` | Show the definition as written instead of the resolved asset |

Examples:

```sh
td2d asset show props/crate --json
td2d asset show props/crate --raw
```

<a id="td2d-asset-emit"></a>

### td2d asset emit

Run a TypeScript asset script and write the definition it returns to assets/<id>/asset.json.

```sh
td2d asset emit [options] <script>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<script>` | Script whose default export is an asset definition, or a function returning one |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--id <id>` | Asset id (default: the id in the definition) |
| `--out <file>` | Write here instead of assets/<id>/asset.json |
| `--overwrite` | Replace an existing file that differs |
| `--print` | Print the definition without writing it |
| `--timeout <ms>` | Stop the script after this long (default 30000) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d asset emit scripts/barrel.ts --json
td2d asset emit scripts/fence.ts --id props/fence --overwrite
```

Scripts import helpers from '@td2d/core/sdk' and run in a separate Node process that may read only the project and the packages it imports: no writes, processes, workers or addons, 512 MB of memory and 30 s by default. The JSON file, not the script, is what td2d generates from.

<a id="td2d-asset-create"></a>

### td2d asset create

Scaffold assets/<id>/asset.json from a template. The result is validated before it is written.

```sh
td2d asset create [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | New asset id, such as props/barrel |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--template <name>` | Asset template (box, character-blockout, cylinder, sphere). Default `"box"`. |
| `--description <text>` | Description to write into the asset |

Examples:

```sh
td2d asset create props/barrel --template cylinder
td2d asset create characters/hero --template character-blockout --json
```

<a id="td2d-generate"></a>

### td2d generate

Run the full pipeline: build the model, render every direction and frame, make sprites and a sheet, validate, and export.

```sh
td2d generate [options] [ids...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[ids...]` | Asset ids (default: every asset) |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--clips <list>` | Render only these clips, comma separated; other frames come from the render cache |
| `--directions <list>` | Render only these directions, comma separated; other frames come from the render cache |
| `--frames <selector>` | Render only these frames (clip/direction/range, such as walk/s/0-2); others come from the render cache. Repeat to add more |
| `--force` | Recompute every stage instead of reusing cached results |
| `--no-cache` | Neither read nor write the stage cache |
| `--dry-run` | Show which stages would run or be reused, without running anything |
| `--strict` | Fail (exit 5) on validation warnings as well as errors |
| `--allow-hardware` | Use the GPU if available. Faster, but output depends on the machine. |
| `--timeout <ms>` | Stop any asset that takes longer than this (E_ASSET_TIMEOUT) |
| `--from <stage>` | Recompute this stage and every later one. One of `resolve`, `model`, `rig`, `plan`, `render`, `pixel`, `sheet`, `validate`, `export`. |
| `--to <stage>` | Stop after this stage. One of `resolve`, `model`, `rig`, `plan`, `render`, `pixel`, `sheet`, `validate`, `export`. |

Examples:

```sh
td2d generate props/crate --json
td2d generate --dry-run
td2d generate props/crate --from render
td2d generate characters/knight --frames walk/s/0-2
```

Stages: resolve, model, plan, render, pixel, sheet, validate, export. Unchanged stages are reused from .td2d/cache. Outputs go to build/<id>/; sheets/ holds <name>.png, <name>.json (Aseprite) and manifest.json. Exit code 5 means the sprites were written but failed validation; read build/<id>/validation.json.

<a id="td2d-batch"></a>

### td2d batch

Generate many assets with a concurrency limit and one shared browser, writing build/batch-report.json. A failure stops the batch unless --continue-on-error.

```sh
td2d batch [options]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--filter <glob>` | Asset ids to include: * within a segment, ** across segments (props/*, characters/**) |
| `--manifest <file>` | A batch manifest: assets with per-asset overrides (td2d schema batch-manifest) |
| `--concurrency <n>` | Assets generated at once (default: cores minus one, at most 4) |
| `--continue-on-error` | Run every asset even after failures; exit 6 if any failed |
| `--fail-fast` | Cancel assets already running when one fails |
| `--resume <report>` | Skip the assets that succeeded in this earlier batch report |
| `--report <file>` | Where to write the batch report (default build/batch-report.json) |
| `--force` | Recompute every stage instead of reusing cached results |
| `--no-cache` | Neither read nor write the stage cache |
| `--dry-run` | Show which stages would run or be reused, without running anything |
| `--strict` | Fail (exit 5) on validation warnings as well as errors |
| `--allow-hardware` | Use the GPU if available. Faster, but output depends on the machine. |
| `--timeout <ms>` | Stop any asset that takes longer than this (E_ASSET_TIMEOUT) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d batch --json
td2d batch --filter "props/*" --continue-on-error --json
td2d batch --manifest release.json --concurrency 4
td2d batch --resume build/batch-report.json
```

Exit codes: 0 all succeeded, 4 the batch stopped at a failure, 6 some failed with --continue-on-error, 130 cancelled.

<a id="td2d-model-build"></a>

### td2d model build

Build the model GLB for an asset, with its rig and baked clips (the resolve, model and rig stages).

```sh
td2d model build [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--force` | Recompute every stage instead of reusing cached results |
| `--no-cache` | Neither read nor write the stage cache |
| `--dry-run` | Show which stages would run or be reused, without running anything |
| `--strict` | Fail (exit 5) on validation warnings as well as errors |
| `--allow-hardware` | Use the GPU if available. Faster, but output depends on the machine. |
| `--timeout <ms>` | Stop any asset that takes longer than this (E_ASSET_TIMEOUT) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d model build props/crate --json
```

<a id="td2d-model-inspect"></a>

### td2d model inspect

Report bounds, triangle counts, materials, parts, bones, clips and glTF validation for an asset model, building it if needed. With --clip, report one clip; add --keys for its keys, including generated ones.

```sh
td2d model inspect [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--clip <name>` | Report one clip |
| `--keys` | With --clip: include every key (a generator shows the keys it made) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d model inspect props/crate --json
td2d model inspect characters/knight --clip walk --keys --json
```

<a id="td2d-rig-list"></a>

### td2d rig list

List rig presets: built in and from presets/rig/.

```sh
td2d rig list [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
td2d rig list --json
```

<a id="td2d-rig-show"></a>

### td2d rig show

Show the bones of an asset rig with their rest positions, and the parts attached to each.

```sh
td2d rig show [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id |

Examples:

```sh
td2d rig show characters/knight --json
```

<a id="td2d-process"></a>

### td2d process

Rerun pixel processing and every later stage from the cached renders. Use it after changing pixel settings: nothing is rendered again unless the renders are missing or out of date.

```sh
td2d process [options] [ids...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[ids...]` | Asset ids (default: every asset) |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--force` | Recompute every stage instead of reusing cached results |
| `--no-cache` | Neither read nor write the stage cache |
| `--dry-run` | Show which stages would run or be reused, without running anything |
| `--strict` | Fail (exit 5) on validation warnings as well as errors |
| `--allow-hardware` | Use the GPU if available. Faster, but output depends on the machine. |
| `--timeout <ms>` | Stop any asset that takes longer than this (E_ASSET_TIMEOUT) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d process props/crate --json
td2d process props/crate --strict
```

Same as `td2d generate <id> --from pixel`. Stages before pixel are reused from .td2d/cache when they are still valid, and run otherwise.

<a id="td2d-sheet"></a>

### td2d sheet

Lay out the sheets again from the cached sprites, then validate and export. Use it after changing sheet settings.

```sh
td2d sheet [options] [ids...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[ids...]` | Asset ids (default: every asset) |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--force` | Recompute every stage instead of reusing cached results |
| `--no-cache` | Neither read nor write the stage cache |
| `--dry-run` | Show which stages would run or be reused, without running anything |
| `--strict` | Fail (exit 5) on validation warnings as well as errors |
| `--allow-hardware` | Use the GPU if available. Faster, but output depends on the machine. |
| `--timeout <ms>` | Stop any asset that takes longer than this (E_ASSET_TIMEOUT) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d sheet characters/knight --json
```

Same as `td2d generate <id> --from sheet`.

<a id="td2d-export"></a>

### td2d export

Write export formats from the cached sheets. With --format, write these formats instead of the ones in the asset (the manifest is always written).

```sh
td2d export [options] [ids...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[ids...]` | Asset ids (default: every asset) |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--format <list>` | Comma-separated formats: aseprite-json, manifest, frames, pixi, phaser-atlas, godot-spriteframes, gif-preview |
| `--force` | Recompute every stage instead of reusing cached results |
| `--no-cache` | Neither read nor write the stage cache |
| `--dry-run` | Show which stages would run or be reused, without running anything |
| `--strict` | Fail (exit 5) on validation warnings as well as errors |
| `--allow-hardware` | Use the GPU if available. Faster, but output depends on the machine. |
| `--timeout <ms>` | Stop any asset that takes longer than this (E_ASSET_TIMEOUT) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d export characters/knight --format pixi,phaser-atlas --json
td2d export --format godot-spriteframes
```

<a id="td2d-render"></a>

### td2d render

Render an asset (pipeline stages up to render) or a GLB file to transparent PNG frames, one per direction and sample time.

```sh
td2d render [options] [id]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[id]` | Asset id: run the pipeline up to the render stage |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--glb <file>` | Render a binary glTF file instead of an asset |
| `--out <dir>` | Output directory for --glb. Must be empty, new, or one td2d created. |
| `--directions <spec>` | With --glb: direction set (d1, d1-side, d4, d8, d16) or compass names (default d4). With an asset id: only these directions, comma separated |
| `--clips <list>` | With an asset id: only these clips, comma separated |
| `--frames <selector>` | With an asset id: only these frames, as clip/direction/range (walk/s/0-2, walk/*/3, idle/*/*). Repeat to add more |
| `--frame <WxH>` | Final sprite size in pixels. Default `{"width":32,"height":32}`. |
| `--supersample <n>` | Render at this multiple of the frame size. Default `4`. |
| `--ppu <n>` | Pixels per metre in the final sprite. Default `16`. |
| `--camera <preset>` | Camera preset. Default `"dimetric"`. |
| `--ground-margin <px>` | Pixels between the pivot line and the bottom edge (overrides the preset) |
| `--lighting <preset>` | Lighting preset. Default `"studio-toon"`. |
| `--clip <name>` | Animation clip to sample |
| `--times <list>` | Clip times in seconds, comma separated (default 0) |
| `--allow-hardware` | Use the GPU if available. Faster, but output depends on the machine. |
| `--force` | With an asset id: recompute instead of reusing cached stages |

Examples:

```sh
td2d render props/crate --json
td2d render characters/knight --clips walk --directions s,w --json
td2d render characters/knight --frames walk/s/0-2 --json
td2d render --glb crate.glb --out frames --directions d8 --json
td2d render --glb hero.glb --out walk --clip walk --times 0,0.1,0.2,0.3 --frame 32x48 --ground-margin 4
```

Frames are written to <out>/<clip or static>/<direction>/<nnn>.png at frame size times supersample.

<a id="td2d-inspect"></a>

### td2d inspect

Summarise the last generation of an asset: sheet, cells, pivot, validation and stages. With --frame, report one sprite.

```sh
td2d inspect [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--frame <key>` | Sprite key such as idle/s/000 |
| `--cells` | List every cell: sheet, rectangle, trim offset and whether it is mirrored |

Examples:

```sh
td2d inspect props/crate --json
td2d inspect props/crate --frame idle/s/000 --json
td2d inspect characters/knight --cells --json
```

<a id="td2d-preview"></a>

### td2d preview

Write an enlarged PNG of the sheet on a visible background with cell borders, for viewing with an image reader.

```sh
td2d preview [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--scale <n>` | Enlargement factor. Default `8`. |
| `--background <value>` | checker, transparent or #rrggbb. Default `"checker"`. |
| `--no-grid` | Leave out cell borders |
| `--out <file>` | Where to write the PNG (default: build/<id>/preview.png) |
| `--overwrite` | Replace --out if it already exists |
| `--clip <name>` | Show one clip: its frames in a row for each direction |
| `--sheet <n>` | With the sheet layout: which sheet to show, counting from 0. Default `0`. |
| `--layout <layout>` | sheet: the whole sheet. ring: one frame per direction, placed at the angle it faces. One of `sheet`, `ring`. Default `"sheet"`. |

Examples:

```sh
td2d preview props/crate --json
td2d preview props/crate --scale 4 --out /tmp/crate.png --overwrite
td2d preview props/crate --layout ring
td2d preview characters/knight --clip walk --scale 4
```

<a id="td2d-history-list"></a>

### td2d history list

List recorded generations of an asset, newest first. A new entry is recorded whenever the outputs change.

```sh
td2d history list [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id |

Examples:

```sh
td2d history list props/crate --json
```

<a id="td2d-history-show"></a>

### td2d history show

Show one recorded generation: its sheets, cells, clips, failing checks, timing and size on disk.

```sh
td2d history show [options] <id> [entry]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id |
| `[entry]` | Entry id, a unique prefix of it or of its hash, "latest" or "previous". Default `"latest"`. |

Examples:

```sh
td2d history show characters/knight --json
td2d history show characters/knight previous
td2d history show characters/knight 9ddbd7dc --json
```

<a id="td2d-history-prune"></a>

### td2d history prune

Remove old history entries: beyond the newest --keep of each asset, older than --older-than, or both. The newest entry of an asset is always kept.

```sh
td2d history prune [options] [ids...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[ids...]` | Asset ids (default: every asset with history, including deleted ones) |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--keep <n>` | Keep this many newest entries of each asset |
| `--older-than <duration>` | Remove entries older than this, such as 30d or 12h |
| `--dry-run` | Report what would be removed without removing it |

Examples:

```sh
td2d history prune --keep 10 --json
td2d history prune characters/knight --older-than 30d --dry-run
```

<a id="td2d-cache-stats"></a>

### td2d cache stats

Size of the cache by stage and item kind, with the oldest and newest use.

```sh
td2d cache stats [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
td2d cache stats --json
```

<a id="td2d-cache-clean"></a>

### td2d cache clean

Remove cache entries by age or size, least recently used first. Nothing in build/ is touched.

```sh
td2d cache clean [options]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--older-than <duration>` | Remove entries not used for this long: 30m, 12h, 1d, 2w |
| `--max-size <size>` | Then remove least recently used entries until the cache fits: 500MB, 5GB |
| `--all` | Remove every entry |
| `--dry-run` | Report what would be removed without removing it |

Examples:

```sh
td2d cache clean --older-than 1d --json
td2d cache clean --max-size 2GB
td2d cache clean --all
```

<a id="td2d-compare"></a>

### td2d compare

Compare the current build of an asset with an earlier generation, cell by cell: changed pixels per cell, added and removed cells, and an optional diff image.

```sh
td2d compare [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Asset id |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--against <entry>` | A history entry id (td2d history list) or a directory. Default: the previous history entry |
| `--out <file>` | Write a PNG with a row per changed cell: before, after and the difference |
| `--threshold <n>` | Colour difference ignored, from 0 (exact, default) to 1. Default `0`. |
| `--scale <n>` | Enlargement of the diff image. Default `4`. |

Examples:

```sh
td2d compare characters/knight --json
td2d compare characters/knight --against 2026-10-02T09-00-00-000Z-1a2b3c4d5e6f --out diff.png
td2d compare props/crate --against ../old/build/props/crate
```

The --out image has a row per changed cell, most changed first (data.diffRows names them), and three columns: before, after, and the changed pixels in red.

<a id="td2d-viewer"></a>

### td2d viewer

Serve the read-only web viewer for this project's build directory until interrupted.

```sh
td2d viewer [options]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--port <n>` | Port to listen on (0 picks a free one). Default `4747`. |
| `--host <host>` | Interface to bind. Default `"127.0.0.1"`. |
| `--open` | Open the viewer in the default browser |
| `--no-watch` | Do not watch build/ for changes: no live reload |
| `--watch-mode <mode>` | native uses fs.watch; poll checks every 200 ms, for mounts that deliver no file events (some Docker and network file systems). One of `native`, `poll`. Default `"native"`. |

Examples:

```sh
td2d viewer --open
td2d viewer --port 0 --json
td2d viewer --watch-mode poll
```

The URL is logged on stderr as soon as the server listens (an NDJSON line with "url" under --json). Stop with Ctrl+C.

<a id="td2d-index"></a>

### td2d index

Write the viewer as a static site into build/ (index.html, index.json and _td2d/) so any static file server can show the build without td2d.

```sh
td2d index [options]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--out <dir>` | Write the site here instead, copying the build outputs it needs |
| `--no-history` | Leave out history entries (the History and Compare tabs are then empty) |

Examples:

```sh
td2d index --json
npx serve build
td2d index --out /tmp/site --no-history
```

<a id="td2d-explain"></a>

### td2d explain

Explain an error or warning code: what it means, when it happens, how to fix it and where to read more.

```sh
td2d explain [options] [code]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[code]` | An error code such as E_ASSET_INVALID or a warning code such as W_FRAME_CLIPPED |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--list` | List every error and warning code with its summary |

Examples:

```sh
td2d explain E_PART_NOT_MANIFOLD
td2d explain w_frame_clipped --json
td2d explain --list --json
```

<a id="td2d-completion"></a>

### td2d completion

Print a shell completion script for bash, zsh or fish: commands, options, option values and asset ids.

```sh
td2d completion [options] <shell>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<shell>` | One of bash, zsh, fish |

Examples:

```sh
eval "$(td2d completion bash)"
eval "$(td2d completion zsh)"
td2d completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/td2d.fish
```
